questions.question: Which hosts belong to the web group in this INI inventory?
options: All three hosts
Only app1
app1 and app2
db1 and app1
questions.explanation: Inventory group headings assign the following hosts to that group until another heading begins.

questions.question: Which built-in inventory group contains every host?
options: default
localhost
all
ungrouped
questions.explanation: all includes every inventory host. ungrouped contains hosts that belong to no other group apart from all.

questions.question: Which hosts does the quoted pattern select?
options: Only a host literally named production
Hosts in either group, including non-overlapping hosts
Hosts present in both web and production
All hosts except web
questions.explanation: The & intersection operator limits the selection to hosts in both groups. Quoting prevents the shell from interpreting special characters.

questions.question: What does ansible.builtin.ping primarily verify for a typical Linux target?
options: That the target’s web application is healthy
That every TCP port is open
ICMP echo reachability only
Ansible connection and usable Python execution on the target
questions.explanation: The Ansible ping module is not network ICMP ping. It exercises the Ansible connection and remote module execution path.

questions.question: Which built-in module normally gathers target system facts?
options: ansible.builtin.setup
ansible.builtin.assert
ansible.builtin.meta
ansible.builtin.copy
questions.explanation: setup gathers facts such as platform and interfaces. These facts can be referenced through ansible_facts during playbook execution.

questions.question: What should you consider when a play uses gather_facts: false but a task reads ansible_facts?
options: Those facts may be unavailable unless collected or supplied another way
Ansible always gathers all facts despite the setting
Every task will run on localhost
ansible_facts becomes the host’s environment automatically
questions.explanation: Disabling automatic fact gathering can save time, but facts must come from another deliberate source before tasks rely on them.

questions.question: What does become: true request for this play?
options: A new SSH key for every task
Permanent root access for every local user
A switch to a different inventory file
Privilege escalation using the configured become method and user
questions.explanation: become requests privilege escalation. Its success depends on the remote account’s configured authorization and any required credentials.
questions.code:
- hosts: web
  become: true
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.package:
        name: nginx
        state: present

questions.question: What is the goal of an idempotent configuration-management task?
options: Every execution must restart the machine
It must never report a failure
Repeated execution converges to the desired state without unnecessary changes
It must only execute once in the lifetime of a host
questions.explanation: Idempotency concerns repeated effects, not simply whether a command runs. Desired-state modules often inspect existing state before changing it.

questions.question: Which module should normally be preferred for running an executable without needing shell operators?
options: ansible.builtin.raw for every Python-capable host
ansible.builtin.command
ansible.builtin.debug
ansible.builtin.shell in all cases
questions.explanation: command avoids shell interpretation, reducing quoting and injection risks. Use shell only when shell features are actually required.

questions.question: Why does this task not create a shell pipeline?
options: Ansible forbids the printf executable
command does not interpret | as a shell operator
The pipe runs only on the controller automatically
command interprets pipes only when become is enabled
questions.explanation: command passes arguments without shell parsing. Use a suitable module or an explicitly justified shell task for pipelines.

questions.question: What does creates accomplish here?
options: Guarantees the command is safe under all conditions
Creates the marker automatically before running the command
Deletes the marker after success
Skips command execution when /opt/app/.initialized already exists
questions.explanation: creates is a guard checked before execution. The command or another task must actually create the marker when initialization succeeds.

questions.question: When is the notified handler normally scheduled?
options: Before the template task runs
Only when the task is skipped
Only when the notifying task reports changed
After every successful task regardless of changed status
questions.explanation: Notifications are driven by changed status. A successful but unchanged task does not normally notify handlers.
questions.code:
- ansible.builtin.template:
    src: app.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/app.conf
  notify: Restart app

questions.question: Three tasks notify the same handler before the handler phase. How many times does it normally run in that phase?
options: Three times in parallel
Once
Once per notification character
It never runs if more than one task notifies it
questions.explanation: Ansible deduplicates handler notifications within a handler execution phase. Handlers run in their defined order rather than notification order.

questions.question: What does this meta task request?
options: Restart the controller process
Run handlers notified so far at this point
Skip all pending tasks permanently
Delete every handler definition
questions.explanation: flush_handlers creates an earlier handler execution point. Later changed tasks may notify the same handlers again.

questions.question: When should you use template rather than copy for a configuration file?
options: When the source contains Jinja expressions that must be rendered
Only when copying a binary image
Whenever the file is larger than one kilobyte
When file permissions must be ignored
questions.explanation: template renders Jinja on the controller before transferring content. copy is appropriate for content that does not require template rendering.

questions.question: Why is the mode quoted in this task?
options: To avoid unintended numeric interpretation and pass the intended permission string
Because every YAML scalar must be quoted
To make the file executable automatically
To encrypt the permission bits
questions.explanation: Quoting permission modes avoids YAML numeric-interpretation surprises. The file module then applies the intended octal mode.

questions.question: Why must a YAML value beginning with {{ commonly be quoted?
options: To make the variable globally immutable
To make it a YAML string containing a Jinja expression
To prevent Jinja from ever evaluating it
To convert the expression into an inventory group
questions.explanation: YAML parses the document before Ansible renders expressions. Quoting avoids confusion with YAML mapping syntax.

questions.question: An inventory variable and an extra variable passed with -e have the same name. Which normally wins?
options: The shorter value
The inventory variable always wins
The extra variable
Whichever appears first alphabetically
questions.explanation: Extra variables have very high variable precedence. Use them deliberately because they can override values from many other variable sources.

questions.question: If optional_port is undefined, what does this expression yield?
options: The number zero
An undefined-variable error in all cases
The string optional_port
questions.explanation: The default filter supplies a fallback for undefined values. Treating empty or false values as missing requires the filter’s optional boolean behavior.

questions.question: Why apply the bool filter when enabled may be a string such as "false"?
options: To make the task run exactly twice
To quote every shell argument
To convert recognized boolean-like values before evaluating the condition
To turn a variable into a fact on all hosts
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion avoids treating a nonempty string as an intended boolean value. Modern conditionals should evaluate to booleans.
questions.code:
- ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: Feature enabled
  when: enabled | bool

questions.question: How are these two when entries combined?
options: They are evaluated only on localhost
The second overrides the first
Both must be true
Either may be true
questions.explanation: A list of when conditions is combined with logical AND. The condition is evaluated for each host executing the task.

questions.question: What does this when expression require?
options: Both must be true
Either maintenance or emergency must evaluate true
Both must be false
Only maintenance is evaluated in all cases
questions.explanation: An explicit or expression expresses alternative conditions. A YAML list of separate conditions would instead use AND.

questions.question: Which loop items run this debug task?
options: Only values greater than 2
Only the first item
No items because when cannot be used with loop
All items because one matches
questions.explanation: A condition on a looping task is evaluated separately for each item.
questions.code:
- ansible.builtin.debug:
    var: item
  loop: [1, 2, 3, 4]
  when: item > 2

questions.question: A task loops over several items and uses register: checks. Where are its per-item results normally stored?
options: hostvars.results for every host automatically
checks.results
checks.stdout contains every item as a dictionary
The inventory file is rewritten with each result
questions.explanation: A registered looping task returns an aggregate result with a results list. Individual module result fields live inside those entries.

questions.question: What is the effect of changed_when: false here?
options: The result is not registered
The command never runs
The return code becomes zero automatically
The task does not report changed even if the command executes
questions.explanation: changed_when controls change reporting. It does not alter execution, erase failures, or make a command idempotent by itself.

questions.question: When does this task fail according to the custom failed_when list?
options: When either condition is true
Never, because failed_when cannot be a list
Whenever stderr is nonempty regardless of the second test
Only when both conditions are true
questions.explanation: A failed_when list combines expressions with AND. Use one expression with or if either condition should independently indicate failure.
questions.code:
register: result
failed_when:
  - result.rc != 0
  - '"FATAL" in result.stderr'

questions.question: What makes this task retry rather than simply executing once?
options: register automatically retries every failed task
changed_when always enables retries
The until condition is checked after an attempt
Every command module task retries by default
questions.explanation: until defines the success condition for retrying this task. retries and delay control the retry budget and waiting period.
questions.code:
- ansible.builtin.command: /opt/app/healthcheck
  register: health
  until: health.rc == 0
  retries: 5
  delay: 2
  changed_when: false

questions.question: Does ignore_errors: true generally make an unreachable host continue as if its SSH connection succeeded?
options: Yes, it converts every connection into local execution
Yes, it repairs the SSH connection
Only if the inventory name contains a dot
No; unreachable errors require separate handling
questions.explanation: ignore_errors applies to ordinary task failure results, not every possible failure mode. Ansible has separate unreachable-host handling.

questions.question: When does a rescue section normally run?
options: When a task in the associated block returns a failed result
Only when every block task succeeds
Before the block starts
For every syntax error anywhere in the playbook
questions.explanation: rescue handles normal block task failures. Invalid task definitions and unreachable hosts are not ordinary rescuable failed results.

questions.question: What is the role of always in an Ansible block?
options: Run its tasks after the block and any rescue in normal block error handling
Prevent any task from failing
Make all tasks run forever
Gather facts before every task
questions.explanation: always is used for actions such as cleanup after block execution. It does not overcome all fatal execution or connectivity problems.

questions.question: Which statement about ansible-playbook --check is accurate?
options: It simulates supported operations, but support and result detail vary by module
It guarantees every application behavior has been tested
Every module executes real changes exactly as usual
It prevents reading any remote state
questions.explanation: Check mode depends on module support and task behavior. Unsupported tasks may be skipped, and registered-result-dependent flows may not simulate fully.

questions.question: Why should you be careful enabling --diff on tasks that render secret-bearing configuration?
options: It permanently disables Ansible Vault
Diff mode always changes file ownership
The before-and-after output can expose sensitive content
Diff mode bypasses SSH authentication
questions.explanation: Diff output can reveal file contents. Use appropriate output controls such as diff: false for sensitive tasks.

questions.question: What does Ansible Vault primarily protect?
options: Encrypted data at rest in files or variables
All target host disks automatically
Every network request made by managed applications
The confidentiality of all decrypted debug output
questions.explanation: Vault protects stored content. Once decrypted for use, secrets still need careful handling in tasks, logs, and application configuration.

questions.question: What does no_log: true aim to prevent for a task?
options: The task from contacting remote hosts
The value from existing in process memory
Sensitive task data appearing in normal Ansible output
Every later task from printing the same secret
questions.explanation: no_log suppresses normal task-result logging. Do not expose the same secret through a separate debug task or assume it solves every logging path.

questions.question: In this delegated task, which host does inventory_hostname normally identify?
options: Every member of the web group at once
The controller’s operating-system hostname
Always 127.0.0.1
The original inventory host the task is executing for
questions.explanation: Delegation changes where the action runs. inventory_hostname still identifies the original host context, though other connection variables can come from the delegated host.

questions.question: A play uses serial: 2 and a task uses run_once: true. How is run_once normally scoped?
options: Once per worker process forever
Once per task loop item on every host
Exactly once for the entire inventory regardless of batching
Once for each serial batch
questions.explanation: run_once normally applies to the current host batch. If an operation truly must run once for the entire play, design its condition accordingly.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of serial in a play?
options: Control the number of loop items per task
Make YAML keys execute alphabetically
Change the SSH port to a serial device
Process hosts in batches instead of all targeted hosts at once
questions.explanation: serial bounds the batch of hosts progressing through the play. It is useful for rolling maintenance and controlled deployments.

questions.question: What does throttle: 1 on a task limit?
options: The total number of hosts in inventory
The command’s CPU frequency
The number of handlers defined in a role
The number of workers executing that task concurrently
questions.explanation: throttle can constrain task concurrency below the broader worker or batch limits. It does not set a permanent host count.

questions.question: How does the free strategy differ from the default linear strategy?
options: Hosts can advance through tasks without waiting for every other host at each task boundary
The inventory becomes read-only
Every task runs on the controller only
Handlers are completely disabled
questions.explanation: free lets hosts progress independently within applicable limits. Cross-host synchronization assumptions that fit linear execution may no longer hold.

questions.question: What does the forks setting primarily control?
options: The number of tasks defined in each role
The number of Git branches checked out
The maximum number of parallel worker processes Ansible uses for host execution
The maximum number of inventory groups
questions.explanation: forks affects parallel host work. serial, throttle, strategy, and target responsiveness can further limit effective concurrency.

questions.question: Which distinction between import_tasks and include_tasks is generally correct?
options: include_tasks cannot use variables
import_tasks is static reuse; include_tasks is dynamic reuse
import_tasks automatically creates a role
Both always execute tasks during inventory parsing
questions.explanation: Static imports are expanded earlier; dynamic includes are processed during execution. This affects conditionals, loops, and tag handling.

questions.question: A dynamic include has a tag, but its included tasks are untagged. What should you consider when selecting tasks by that tag?
options: Tags are only valid on handlers
The include’s tag is not automatically inherited by all included tasks
Selecting a tag disables every include
All included tasks always inherit it
questions.explanation: Dynamic includes need deliberate tag propagation, such as apply tags or tagging the included tasks. Tagging the include alone is not blanket inheritance.

questions.question: Where should a reusable role normally place variables that callers are expected to override easily?
options: A hardcoded shell command string
defaults/main.yml
meta/main.yml only
handlers/main.yml
questions.explanation: Role defaults have low variable precedence and are designed for customization. Role vars have higher precedence and are harder for callers to override.

questions.question: What does listen allow in a handler definition?
options: Subscribe a handler to a notification topic independent of its name
Make a handler run unconditionally
Gather facts from every inventory group
Open a TCP port on the managed host
questions.explanation: listen topics decouple notifications from individual handler names. Multiple handlers can listen to the same topic.

questions.question: Why use ansible.builtin.copy instead of an ambiguous short module name in shared playbooks?
options: It disables all module argument checks
It encrypts the copied file by default
It guarantees the file is copied only once
It identifies the intended collection and module explicitly
questions.explanation: Fully qualified collection names clarify module resolution and reduce collisions with similarly named modules from other collections.

questions.question: What does hostvars["db1"]["service_port"] access when that host and variable exist?
options: The controller’s local environment variable
The service_port variable for inventory host db1
An SSH connection to db1 that runs automatically
Only the currently targeted host’s operating-system port
questions.explanation: hostvars exposes inventory-host variable contexts. Reading gathered facts from another host still requires those facts to be available.

questions.question: What does this environment setting apply to?
options: The environment of the task executed on its target host
Every later playbook invocation automatically
The inventory file’s YAML parser
The controller’s permanent shell environment
questions.explanation: The environment keyword supplies environment variables for task execution. It does not permanently modify the controller or target account’s login configuration.

questions.question: What does poll: 0 request for an async task?
options: Run synchronously with no timeout
Poll every zero milliseconds until completion
Cancel the task immediately
Start it asynchronously without waiting for completion in that task
questions.explanation: poll zero is fire-and-forget behavior for the launching task. Use the returned job information to inspect or wait for completion separately.

questions.question: Which module checks the result of a job launched with async and poll: 0?
options: ansible.builtin.set_stats always
ansible.builtin.async_status
ansible.builtin.add_host
ansible.builtin.wait_for_connection only
questions.explanation: async_status uses the async job ID to retrieve status. A polling loop with until can wait for its finished result.

questions.question: What does this task enforce?
options: The desired replicas value must be greater than zero
It creates that many replicas automatically
It silently skips all later tasks when the assertion passes
It converts replicas to zero on failure
questions.explanation: assert checks preconditions and produces a failure if its expression is false. Validation is distinct from actually provisioning the desired resource.
questions.code:
- ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - replicas | int > 0
    fail_msg: replicas must be positive
